messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change the person's action in the source video to match the action demonstrated in the motion reference. Transfer only the demonstrated action; do not adopt the reference person's appearance, the reference scene, or the reference camera setup. Preserve all other aspects of the current video, including the person's identity, appearance, scene, lighting, and camera framing.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Only compare editing requirements; historical appearance words are not observed facts.","original_user_request":"Using the provided source video, apply the following edit: Please change the person's action to match the reference video. Transfer only the demonstrated action, not the reference person's appearance or the reference scene and camera setup. Preserve all other aspects of the current video.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The man stands in profile, then turns toward the camera, raises his arms to adjust his vest and collar, and finally stands facing right again.","camera":"Medium full shot at eye level, mostly static with a slight zoom or reframe as the subject moves closer.","clothing":"White long-sleeved collared shirt, black vest, red trousers, and black shoes.","hair_color":"Dark brown or black.","hairstyle":"Short hair with a small top-knot or bun on top of the head.","identity":"A 3D-rendered man with a dark complexion, slim build, and a small top-knot hairstyle.","scene":"An outdoor amusement park or fairground at dusk, with a covered structure lined with round lights, a red and blue striped barrier, a small red cart, and a striped awning in the background."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The man's action was altered from the source's head-touching/turning motion to a new sequence: he stands, turns slightly, raises his arms to adjust his vest and collar, then returns to a standing profile. His clothing, hairstyle, fairground scene, lighting, and overall framing remain consistent with the source.
arguments.requested_change: Change the man's action to match the motion reference, while preserving his identity, clothing, scene, lighting, and camera framing.
uncertain: Whether the intended reference motion was fully captured is unclear because the output action differs noticeably from the visible reference sequence.
unexpected_changes: The new action does not clearly reproduce the reference's distinctive forward-leaning, hand-to-face, and arm-crossing motion; it instead resembles a vest/collar adjustment.
